resources.string: Account listening history from all connected devices. Refreshes when you open your profile or tap Refresh.
Your ID, listening history and preferences belong to this account. Create it offline and connect it to different servers.
Keep a recovery file or code separately from this phone. The file also preserves access to servers that still use a previous account key.

Store all 43 characters safely. This code grants account access; do not share it. It needs the account document on this phone or a trusted server. After a reset, save the recovery file too: it retains previous keys for other servers.
Reset password and revoke old access

Choose a recovery file, or enter your ID and recovery code. Recovery keeps the account UUID and creates a new key. An online reset signs out all devices on the selected server. Connect to other servers using the current password to update their old keys. Save the new recovery file after each reset.
This restores local access. Server copies are not revoked offline. When you connect with the current password, the app can update a server that still uses a retained previous key.
The recovery history already contains eight previous keys. No key was removed and the reset was stopped. Keep your current recovery file.
This server uses a key missing from this recovery history. Use the recovery file that includes that key; an already revoked key cannot regain server access.
Open the server connection screen and confirm the trusted server before recovery.
The previous connection expired and was released. Select and trust the server, then sign in again.
The connection result needs verification. Retry to restore the same session.
Check your account ID and password. If no password has been set, configure it in Account first.
Account operation could not be completed. Check your ID, password and server connection. An account with a different identity cannot be linked.
